title: Filter chip row
description: A list page's filters as one line of chips (icon, label, chevron; solid with the value or count when on). Each chip opens a small multi-select popover, a switch chip toggles; the row scrolls sideways with ‹ › when it overflows, shows “Xoá lọc” while a filter is on and ends with the view tools. State in the URL with useFilterParams or the filterParams helpers.
when: The filters of a list, grid or table page on desktop and iPad (md+), under its SearchPill in a StickyContextBar.
Facets with a few to a few dozen values each (status, channel, owner, country), more than one value at a time.

instead.need: One choice among 2–5 views of the same list
A facet with hundreds of values (a customer, a product)

a11y: Every chip is a button: a multi chip has aria-haspopup=dialog and aria-expanded (its popover traps nothing, Escape returns focus to the chip); a switch chip has aria-pressed.
An active chip's name says the filter and its value (“Quốc gia: Đức”, or “Quốc gia · 2”); the options are named checkboxes in a group named after the filter.
The ‹ › buttons are for the pointer only (aria-hidden, out of the tab order): Tab reaches every chip and scrolls it into view.
notes: One line, never wrapping rows of chips (C-032 L3); more than one row → this row.

URL format: one repeated param per filter (?f.status=new&f.status=won&f.big=1); unknown values from an old link are dropped. useFilterParams reads location after mount (prerender-safe) and pushes a history entry per change, so Back undoes a filter.
With Next's router of your own: readFilters(useSearchParams(), specs) in, router.push(`?${writeFilters(params, { status: [...] }, specs)}`) out.
